title: Reading Drill — Recording historic street names — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Recording historic street names — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Elmbrook, work on names disappearing from signs when roads are rebuilt had already produced a small collection of property registers. The town archivist used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the number of names retained.

**B** The group kept a register of alternate names for the new trial, which was planned to run for ten weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that mergers of adjacent streets should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
